mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger is present but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the combined trigger occurs but returns are not significantly below baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is present (p > 0.10), or the trigger is present but returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, coupled with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS), signals supply-side stress that reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months AND RSAFS < previous 12-month average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the combined trigger fails to produce statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% for three consecutive months signals an aggressive easing cycle, reducing risk-free rates and increasing the relative attractiveness of equities, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when this trigger is met (p > 0.10), or the trigger is present but returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA AND HOUST > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies exceed their 12-month MA (p > 0.10), or the trigger is present but returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when this trigger is present (p > 0.10), or the trigger is present but returns are negative in more than 20% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index above 4% for four consecutive months, coupled with a concurrent increase in the federal funds rate, signals an inflationary environment with restrictive monetary policy, which compresses real earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4.0% for 4 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS rising for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both CPI > 4% and FEDFUNDS are rising (p > 0.10), or the trigger is present but returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.
